Potential other name: Hype-Grunge, named after 'Hype!', a documentary reviewing the media hype & corporate appropriation surrounding grunge in the early 1990s.

It's the ubiquitous 'corporate' grunge look derived mainly from experimental 'grunge typography' works by designers like David Carson & Neville Brody and publications like Raygun & Emigre, but diluted & appropriated for more mainstream commercial applications. Some ties to CSA/Industrial Americana, imagery of American industrial decay, and the style of collage-y, dirty, punk/riot grrl zine culture.

Note: Some of the examples here, like Raygun Magazine, wouldn't be considered 'corporate grunge' in the sense that they're not part of the corporate/media marketing version of 'grunge', but they're important to include here since they were extremely influential on the look that the 'grunge' media/hype/corporate marketing machine adopted.
